steps.title: Generation of electrophile
steps.explanation: Concentrated nitric acid reacts with concentrated sulfuric acid. The sulfuric acid protonates nitric acid, which then loses water to generate the electrophile, the nitronium ion (NO2+).
steps.key_point: Sulfuric acid acts as a catalyst here — it is regenerated later in the mechanism, not consumed.

steps.title: Attack on aromatic ring
steps.explanation: The electrophile attacks the electron-rich benzene ring, forming a sigma complex.
steps.key_point: The aromaticity is temporarily lost in this step.

steps.title: Formation of arenium ion
steps.explanation: The sigma complex, called the arenium ion (or Wheland intermediate), is a resonance-stabilized carbocation where the positive charge is delocalized over three carbon atoms of the ring.
steps.key_point: The arenium ion is stabilized by resonance across three ring positions, but it is not aromatic.

steps.title: Deprotonation
steps.explanation: A base, typically the bisulfate ion (HSO4-), removes a proton from the sp3 carbon bearing the nitro group. This reforms the ring's double bond and restores aromaticity.
steps.key_point: Losing the proton restores the stable aromatic sextet of electrons, which makes this step strongly favored.

steps.title: Regeneration of catalyst
steps.explanation: The proton removed in the previous step combines with HSO4- to reform H2SO4, regenerating the catalyst and completing the reaction with nitrobenzene as the final product.
steps.key_point: Sulfuric acid is not consumed overall — it is regenerated, confirming its role as a catalyst rather than a reactant.
